title: Uniform Source Stability for Wilson Fermions
content: We prove source-stability bounds for Wilson lattice gauge theory with degenerate sea-quark pairs, at arbitrary gauge coupling and hopping parameters 0 < κf ≤ κ* < 1/6. For signed, gauge-dependent spatial sources of finite canonical cost, a determinant-minor expansion gives quadratic total-variation control of the full normalized gauge law without a uniform Dirac spectral gap. The same sea pair controls the corresponding fermionic source coefficients. Two identical original pairs give quartic forward relative entropy, and quartic bounds in both directions for nonnegative sources. Determinant models locate the limits of one-pair control, including a cubic entropy law at a regular zero. Spatial heat kernels give uniform costs at fixed positive smearing and an explicit joint source-removal schedule. For overlap fermions, separated-time source coefficients admit exact contact conversion; the full-spacetime Hilbert–Schmidt contact has a sharp smearing threshold. A sharp background-uniform Wilson propagation bound gives explicit energy floors for vacuum-generated flavor-charge sectors when κf < 1/8. A certificate using three positive-time correlations detects finite-energy spectral weight. These results extend source comparison beyond convergent hopping expansions and identify the physical information that a nontrivial continuum limit must retain.
